overview.text: Sydney is the capital of New South Wales, on Australia’s east coast; its wider metropolitan region, Greater Sydney, had the largest population among Australia’s capital-city regions in 2021. The city’s historic center grew around Sydney Cove on Port Jackson, where the British First Fleet arrived in 1788 and established a convict settlement. Sydney’s story also includes much older Aboriginal histories: the Sydney Opera House site at Bennelong Point is on Tubowgule, acknowledged by the Opera House as Gadigal Country. Danish architect Jørn Utzon designed the Opera House, whose sculptural shell-like roof forms evoke harbour sails and have become a defining city landmark.

key_facts.text: Sydney is New South Wales’s capital and lies on the state’s eastern coast.
In the 2021 Census, Greater Sydney had a larger population than any other Australian Greater Capital City Statistical Area.
The British settlement was established in 1788 around Sydney Cove after the First Fleet entered Port Jackson; Sydney was incorporated as a city in 1842.
The Opera House acknowledges its site, Tubowgule at Bennelong Point, as Gadigal Country; Bennelong Point is named for Woollarawarre Bennelong of the Wangal people.
Danish architect Jørn Utzon won the Opera House design competition in 1957; its shell-shaped roofs were designed to evoke Sydney’s harbour sails and cliffs.
